title: Cross It

source.quote: communication is broken off when a crossed transaction occurs

setting: Monday, 9:40. The release slipped on Friday and the team is still feeling it. Arjun, a developer, is at the standing desk, not looking up.

L1.line: You're always on my case. Nothing I do is ever enough for you.
L1.question: He says it flatly, shoulders hunched, not looking up. Which ego state is Arjun speaking from?

options.feedback: The content sounds like a standard he's judging her against, but content isn't the tell here.
Adult would be measured and specific, not "always" / "never" delivered flat and hunched.
Right. The words "always" and "never", the flat tone, and the hunch are Child cues.

L1.lesson: The words "always" and "never", the flat tone, the hunch are Child cues; the content (a complaint about standards) could sound Parental - diagnose from cues, not content.

L2.intro: You (Priya) want this to land Adult-to-Adult, not turn into a slammed door. What do you say back?

beats.line: You're always on my case. Nothing I do is ever enough for you.

options.text: Don't take that tone with me.
options.outcome: "See? Exactly." He turns back to his screen, door-slam energy. The scene ends there.
options.lesson: Parent -> Child is complementary to his opening, so it continues the fight - complementary is not the same as healthy.

options.text: I'm not on your case, I just want the release to ship.
options.outcome: Arjun shrugs. "Sure. Whatever." He stays small.
options.lesson: Adult words, but the "I just" is defensive; the cross is weak because the psychological level still answers his accusation.

options.text: Something's off this morning. What happened on Friday from where you sat?
options.outcome: A pause. Arjun looks up. "The API spec changed Thursday night and nobody told us." Adult-Adult established.
options.lesson: A crossed transaction (Adult -> Adult in reply to Child -> Parent) breaks the loop; Berne's rule 2 - communication stops until someone shifts; Karpman's options - you may answer from any state, not the one addressed.

options.text: Hey, it's okay, I know you're trying.
options.outcome: Arjun softens but stays small. "Thanks... I'll try harder."
options.lesson: Nurturing Parent -> Child is comforting and keeps him in Child; useful once, costly as a pattern (sets up Look How Hard I've Tried).

fields.label: Draw the vectors for Arjun's opening line, and for the best L2 response.
In under 60 words: why is "Hey, it's okay, I know you're trying" a complementary transaction, and why is that the problem?

echo.setting: 48 hours later: a WhatsApp message from a sibling.
